Project Bornomala — tokenizer field guide

Three ways to cut বাংলা into tokens.

Every language model reads Bengali through a tokenizer first. Here are three that exist today, run on the same real sentence: an industry-standard subword tokenizer, Bornomala's own v1, and BMBT — the grammar-first tokenizer built to replace it. Every token boundary on this page comes from real trained tokenizers, run on real Bengali text — nothing here is a mockup.

01 · An industry-standard tokenizer

byte-level BPE, script-blind

mBERT, XLM-RoBERTa, GPT-4o's o200k, DeepSeek's tokenizer — almost every widely-deployed tokenizer today is a byte- or character-level BPE trained across 100+ languages at once. It has no idea Bengali is an abugida, no idea what a conjunct is. It just counts which byte sequences repeat most often, globally — and Bengali gets a thin slice of that shared vocabulary.

Real numbers, measured on held-out Bengali Wikipedia, not estimated: mBERT breaks 18.0% of Bengali conjuncts; XLM-R breaks 10.2%; Sarvam-1 breaks 11.9%; DeepSeek-V3 breaks 28.5%. GPT-4o's o200k fares best of this group on raw fertility (2.608) but fragmentation isn't measurable the same way for it (no open vocabulary to inspect). Being aimed at Indic scripts is not by itself enough: BrahmicTokenizer-131K, built specifically as an Indic-capable drop-in replacement for o200k and carrying more than twice our vocabulary budget, still lands at 2.620 fertility and breaks 22.1% of conjuncts. Full methodology: benchmarks/bengali-comparison.md.

02 · Bornomala v1 — bn-bpe-64k

grapheme-cluster-aware BPE

v1 fixes the one thing that matters most: it never tears a conjunct apart. Before any merge is learned, the text is split into Unicode grapheme clusters — whole rendered units, via the UAX #29 standard — and each whole cluster becomes one indivisible atom. BPE then compresses atoms, not bytes. The structure is discovered statistically; the guarantee is architectural, fixed, load-bearing.

Real, measured, held-out Bengali Wikipedia: fertility 1.524 vs IndicBERTv2's 1.652 (its closest rival), fragmentation 0.01% vs IndicBERTv2's 4.40% — holds across all four registers tested (Wikipedia, literary/formal, general web, news), not just one. v1 is unchanged and still the model published to Hugging Face.

03 · BMBT — Bornomala's Bengali Tokenizer

grammar-first, v2

BMBT doesn't discover Bengali's structure by counting — it parses it. Bengali's akshara (orthographic syllable) is generated by a regular, Unicode-standardized grammar: Consonant (Virama Consonant)* Matra? Modifier*. A finite-state machine reads that grammar directly, verified against Unicode's own Indic_Conjunct_Break rules — like ink finding its own channel through the shape of each letter, rather than a ruler laid on top of it.

Honest result: BMBT ties v1 exactly on fertility, STRR, bytes/token, and fragmentation, across all four held-out registers. Not a win. This matches the design's own formal proof (FORMAL_SPEC.md): a BPE constrained to respect akshara boundaries cannot beat an unconstrained BPE on raw token count — and since akshara boundaries already sit almost exactly where grapheme-cluster boundaries do on well-formed Bengali, the constraint barely bites in practice. What BMBT actually adds is below.

featurize() — take ক্ষুদ্র ("small") apart into what it's actually made of. v1 cannot do this; its atoms are opaque cluster strings with no internal structure to read.

Open frontier, not yet shipped: a small-scale experiment run alongside this page split each akshara's onset (the consonant chain) from its tail (matra + modifiers) into two separate atoms instead of one fused atom — only possible because BMBT already parses that boundary. At matched vocabulary and corpus (8,000 tokens, 3,000 Wikipedia articles, a deliberate proof-of-concept, not the headline 64k run), fertility moved from 1.9587 (fused) to 1.8700 (split) — a real, measured improvement, not yet retrained at production scale.

why v1 still ships

It is the fully measured, HarfBuzz-validated, Hugging-Face-published result. Nothing about BMBT changes it — v1's artifact, weights, and benchmarks are untouched.

why BMBT exists anyway

Fertility is a tie, stated plainly, not a win dressed up. What BMBT buys instead is a real structural output — featurize() — and a grammar that doesn't depend on trusting a generic Unicode library's judgment call. Morphology, the part that could actually move fertility, is deferred, not abandoned.

Project Bornomala — a non-commercial Bengali-first research effort. Every number on this page is measured, not estimated; see bengali-tokenizer/benchmarks/bengali-comparison.md and bengali-tokenizer/docs/bmbt-architecture.md in the repository for full methodology.
